scope.flow: WERC7575Vault::_withdraw (called by withdraw() and redeem()) third-party withdrawal authorization
scope.environment: SukukFi WERC7575Vault and WERC7575ShareToken with validator-signed self-permits

statements.text: The validator private key is compromised (e.g., via phishing or insider attack).
The validator is the only entity capable of signing self-permits on behalf of users.
The owner has previously executed a self-permit so that allowance(owner, owner) > 0.
The attacker uses the compromised validator key to sign and call permit(owner, owner, type(uint256).max, ...) for each user.
The attacker calls vault.withdraw(assets, attacker, user) or vault.redeem(shares, attacker, user) for each user in the same block.

The internal _withdraw function only enforces the self-allowance mechanism and omits the standard third-party authorization check that should be performed when msg.sender != owner, so any caller can withdraw or redeem on behalf of an owner who has a positive self-allowance.
When msg.sender != owner, a third-party withdrawal or redemption must require explicit user approval rather than relying only on the owner's self-allowance.

ambiguities: Report does not state whether the owner's self-permit exists before the attacker's permit call or is created by it; the positive self-allowance is treated as a conditional prior state.
The exact third-party authorization check semantics (e.g., allowance(owner, msg.sender)) are only implied by the mitigation reference, not fully specified.
Timing of setValidator reaction relative to the attack is described only qualitatively.
